attack_technique: Network Denial of Service: Direct Network Flood
description: Adversaries may attempt to cause a denial of service (DoS) by degrading or blocking the availability of services to users by targeting network and system resources with a high volume of direct network traffic, specifically utilizing the User Datagram Protocol (UDP) to overwhelm the target's processing capacity.

patterns.description: Anomalies related to the sheer volume and speed of incoming data packets.

features.name: Extreme Packet Rate
features.description: A massive spike in the number of packets transmitted per second (Flow Pkts/s and Bwd Pkts/s), designed to exhaust the network bandwidth or processing resources of the target.

features.name: Asymmetric Packet Flow
features.description: A highly unbalanced flow where the number of incoming packets (Total Bwd Pkts) overwhelmingly exceeds any outgoing responses from the target, indicating a one-way flood.

patterns.description: Network traffic patterns related to connection intervals and flow duration.

features.name: Microsecond Inter-Arrival Time
features.description: The mean time between successive packets (Flow IAT Mean) drops to near-zero. Packets arrive back-to-back without the natural pauses seen in legitimate user traffic.

features.name: Short-Lived Aggressive Flows
features.description: The overall duration of individual network flows (Flow Duration) is often exceptionally short because the attacker sends a rapid burst of packets without waiting for or establishing a stateful connection.

patterns.description: Anomalies found within the transport layer protocols and port selection.

features.name: Connectionless UDP Dominance
features.description: A sudden, overwhelming dominance of UDP protocol traffic in the network, taking advantage of its connectionless nature to send data without a three-way handshake.

features.name: Randomized/Exhaustive Port Targeting
features.description: Traffic is directed at a wide, random array of destination ports (often represented as Port 0 in aggregations) to force the target server to check for listening applications and generate ICMP Destination Unreachable responses.

patterns.description: Contextual indicators to separate malicious floods from legitimate high-volume traffic.

features.name: Source IP Spoofing
features.description: The flood often originates from highly randomized, spoofed source IP addresses to mask the attacker's identity and prevent simple IP-based blocking.

features.name: Contextual Misalignment (False Positive Filtering)
features.description: The high-volume UDP traffic lacks the behavioral context of legitimate heavy UDP usage, such as online gaming servers, VoIP communications, or media streaming platforms.
